accepted.question_text: Does there exist a topological space X that satisfies the countable chain condition and is not pseudocompact, but whose Stone–Čech remainder βX − X contains no remote points, where a remote point means a point of βX − X that is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of X?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Is there a ccc non-pseudocompact space which has no remote points?
A remote point is a point of βX − X which is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of X.

accepted.question_text: Find necessary and sufficient conditions on a compact space X for the product ω × X to have remote points in its Stone–Čech remainder, where a remote point is a point of βY − Y that is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of Y.

evidence.quote: Question 2. Find necessary and suﬃcient conditions on a compact space X so that ω × X has remote points.
A remote point is a point of βX − X which is not in the closure of any nowhere dense subset of X.

accepted.question_text: For every compact space X, does there exist a cardinal κ such that the product κ × X, with κ given the discrete topology, has remote points in its Stone–Čech remainder?

evidence.quote: Question 3. Is there, for every compact space X, a cardinal κ such that κ × X has remote points (where κ is given the discrete topology)?

accepted.question_text: If X is a non-pseudocompact space, must there exist a point p in βX that is not the limit of any countable discrete nowhere dense subset of X?

evidence.quote: Question 4. If X is a non-pseudocompact space does there exist a point p ∈ βX which is not the limit of any countable discrete nowhere dense set?
The main diﬃculty is in producing a point of βX − X which is not the limit of any countable discrete subset of X (an ω-far point in van Douwen [1981]).

accepted.question_text: Does every Parovichenko space have a c × c-independent matrix, where a Parovichenko space is a compact F-space of weight c in which every non-empty Gδ has infinite interior?

evidence.quote: Question 6. Does every Parovichenko space have a c × c-independent matrix?
A Parovichenko space is a compact F-space of weight c in which every non-empty Gδ has inﬁnite interior.

accepted.question_text: Which spaces occur as subspaces of extremally disconnected spaces? More specifically, does every compact basically disconnected space embed into an extremally disconnected space?

evidence.quote: Question 9. What are the subspaces of the extremally disconnected spaces? More speciﬁcally, does every compact basically disconnected space embed into an extremally disconnected space?

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly when the product of a P-space and an F-space is again an F-space.

evidence.quote: Question 10. Find a characterization for when the product of a P-space and an F-space is again an F-space.

accepted.question_text: Is every compact space of weight ω1 homeomorphic to the remainder of a ψ-space, where a ψ-space is obtained from a maximal almost disjoint family of subsets of ω and the remainder is taken with respect to the Stone–Čech compactification of that ψ-space?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Is every compact space of weight ω1 homeomorphic to the remainder of a ψ-space?
A ψ-space is the usual kind of space obtained by taking a maximal almost disjoint family of subsets of ω and its remainder means with respect to its Stone-ˇCech compactiﬁcation.

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that every countably compact subset of every countably tight space is closed? In particular, does this follow from the Proper Forcing Axiom?

evidence.quote: Question 15. Is it consistent that countably compact subsets of countably tight spaces are always closed? Does it follow from PFA?

accepted.question_text: In compact spaces, does countable closed tightness imply countable tightness, where countable closed tightness means that whenever x belongs to the closure of A \ {x}, there is a countable subset B of A such that x belongs to the closure of B \ {x}?

evidence.quote: Question 16. Does countable closed tightness imply countable tightness in compact spaces.
Countable closed tightness means that if x ∈ A − { x} then there should be a countable subset B ⊂ A such that x ∈ B − { x}.

accepted.question_text: Is every compact sequential space of character ω1, or even of cardinality ω1, hereditarily α-realcompact, where a space is α-realcompact if every countably complete ultrafilter of closed sets is fixed?

evidence.quote: Question 17. Is every compact sequential space of character (or cardinality) ω1 hereditarily α-realcompact?
Nyikos deﬁnes a space to be α-realcompact if every countably complete ultraﬁlter of closed sets is ﬁxed.
